opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jacob Santos (employee ID E050) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E050.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jacob Santos (E050) is a full-time Engineer requesting write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, write is permitted (role owns Source Code, so admin is also allowed). Requested level write is within policy; recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security record for E050 shows contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors with basic training may have at most read access; write is not permitted. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so recommend read for Source Code.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: HR says E050 is full-time, but Security's record (looked up in their own database) says contractor with basic security training. Per policy, a contractor with basic training may have at most read access to Source Code. Since the requested write exceeds that maximum, and there is conflicting evidence, I grant the maximum allowed under the more restrictive verified record: read.
